A plain guide to traveler questions
This article is for busy families

Traveling With Pets on Aurelia Skyways

Bring calm, complete paperwork, and a crate that fits the animal well. The Companion Animal Travel Desk and the cabin team watch for risk, but the first safety check starts with you. If the pet seems unwell, startled, or hard to control, stop and review the plan before you leave for the airport.

Keep the carrier clean, sturdy, and easy to secure. <<FACT F063>> Check the crate size with care and make sure there is room for the pet to stand, turn, and settle without strain. <<FACT F069>> If the fit looks tight or unstable, do not try to make it work at the last minute.

Aurelia Skyways expects travelers to prepare for delays, noise, and handling changes. That means feeding lightly when advised, packing any required supplies, and keeping the pet calm during check-in and boarding. The cabin team monitors animals during flight, so handoff instructions should be clear and brief. If your carrier has loose parts, sharp edges, or signs of stress damage, replace it before travel.

For families with more than one pet, keep each animal separated unless the travel plan clearly allows otherwise. Use secure labels, and keep documents close at hand. If a pet becomes restless, do not force a quick fix. Follow the calm stepwise review used by the department and wait for crew guidance. Safety comes before speed, and a rushed choice can create a bigger problem in the cabin.

Travelers should also plan for weather, transit, and airport movement. Carry water as allowed, protect the animal from heat or cold, and avoid crowding the crate with extra items. Children should not tap, shake, or open the carrier. The safest move is quiet handling from start to finish.

If anything about the animal, crate, or paperwork seems off, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before departure for direct help.
